key_insight: LEAP combines a domain-specialized LLM with active learning to prioritize perovskite precursor additives in a closed loop, using literature-grounded mechanistic descriptors to guide discovery under low-data conditions.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce trial-and-error screening by ranking chemically feasible additives more intelligently, supporting faster optimization of perovskite solar cell performance.
method: Train an LLM on perovskite additive literature to extract mechanism-relevant knowledge.
Convert candidate molecules into interpretable descriptors for downstream scoring.
Use Bayesian optimization plus expert feasibility review for iterative, uncertainty-aware prioritization.
evidence_signal: On unseen literature, the domain-specialized model outperformed general-purpose models in mechanism-consistent reasoning, and the closed-loop proof-of-concept improved average device PCEs across later screening rounds to 20.13% and 20.87% versus 19.25% for control, with a 21.32% champion device.
watch_item: The approach depends on literature quality, expert review, and limited experimental validation, so broader generalization and real-world robustness still need confirmation.
paper_title: LEAP: A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery
